text:
maria: heads-up — during vuln triage I found the on-prem agent (customer: ACME staging) exposing a local management endpoint at 127.0.0.1:2379 that accepts unauthenticated calls. KMS proxying is possible from that endpoint. high risk for key exfil if a jumpbox is compromised.
jess: ouch. can you paste a minimal repro and severity?
maria: repro is simple: exec into agent pod, `curl http://127.0.0.1:2379/keys` -> 200 + JSON. severity: high for pinned-onprem installs.
kevin: is this the legacy agent v1.3 that we deprecated last quarter?
maria: yes — customer has pinned. mitigation we rolled earlier (disable mgmt by default) didn't apply because of pin.
ryan: immediate mitigation suggestions: add a NetworkPolicy to deny all egress from agent pods except to internal KMS service; restrict service account perms to minimal KMS calls; enable audit logging on the KMS proxy so we can see any `GET /keys` calls. also rotate any exposed keys.
jess: i can push a canary netpol to the customer's cluster if they give access. we should also add an admission webhook preventing agent images < v1.4.
kevin: agree on netpol. also recommend enforcing mTLS between agent and KMS, and enforce VPC-level egress whitelist so nodes can't talk to public KMS endpoints.
sec-bot: [automated] created security ticket SEC-2026-1893 for "onprem agent mgmt endpoint exposure". priority: P0.
maria: plan: 1) immediate netpol + RBAC tighten 2) require customer to rotate KMS keys and enable audit streaming to our secure sink 3) ship hotfix (v1.4.1) with management endpoint disabled by default + mTLS 4) schedule forced upgrade for non-compliant pinned installs after legal review.
ryan: i'll own the incident runbook. ETA: can push netpol if customer approves in ~30m. i'll prepare a short pre-approved command bundle.
jess: i'll draft the support note and customer communication. we should include exact logs we need from them and postmortem template.
kevin: additional artifacts: capture node iptables dump, VPC flow logs for suspicious egress, and KMS audit trail (request_id list).
maria: minimal audit fields we need: `timestamp`, `src_ip`, `service_account`, `pod_name`, `path`, `response_code`, `kms_key_id`, `request_body_sha256`. route those to splunk/secure-sink and tie to SEC-2026-1893.
ryan: noted. also add a defensive admission policy snippet to block agent containers running as `privileged` or with hostNetwork enabled.
jess: question for legal/compliance — for pinned customers do we have authority to force upgrades in urgent security cases? currently policy requires opt-in; legal needs to sign off on emergency forced upgrade clause.
maria: for now we'll offer a hotfix and a one-time assisted upgrade. escalate legal asap for policy change.
kevin: quick netpol snippet for k8s (canary):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: agent-eject-restrict
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          redwood-kms: "internal"
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
kevin: and minimal kubectl to apply and label: `kubectl -n redwood apply -f canary-netpol.yaml && kubectl label ns redwood-kms redwood-kms=internal`
sec-bot: [automated] incident created INC-2026-0789 (owner: ryan). paging oncall.
deploy-bot: [automated] flagged customer cluster acme-staging for manual intervention; preventing autopromote for pinned clusters.
ryan: pager ack. assigning roles: triage (maria), mitigation (kevin), customer comms (jess), postmortem (ryan).
maria: i'll write the runbook steps (mitigation checklist + audit queries + escrowed keys rotation) and paste a gist in 15m. for now action items: netpol canary, RBAC service account change, KMS key rotate, enable audit shipping.
jess: i'll include a step for support to get `kubectl logs` and `kubectl exec` output for the agent pod and instructions to verify netpol applied.
kevin: once mitigations are in, recommend we add an automated regression test in CI that fails builds if agent exposes management ports on loopback without auth.
ryan: agreed. postmortem owner: me. target: public postmortem in 5 business days.
maria: thanks everyone. i'll update SEC-2026-1893 and INC-2026-0789 after the canary run. :white_check_mark:
